title: Suárez agrees contact-latria is speculative, not for common public use—prefer absolute inferior cult for her own holiness and maternity
source_text: XXXVIII. Cui doctrinae consentanea sunt quae leguntur apud Franciscum Suarez celeberrimum quoque Jesuitam. Inquirens enim ob quam potissimum rationem Beata Virgo sit adoranda, docet triplicem posse rationem adorationis in Virgine intelligi. Et primam rationem, propter quam Virgo potest adorari, dicit esse extrinsecam, qualis in cruce, vel clavis Christi reperitur. Sicut enim, inquit, crux, & Christum tetigit, & instrumentum fuit nostrae Redemptionis, ita multo perfectius Beatissima Virgo, & Christum tetigit, & ad nostram Redemptionem est cooperata. Hoc igitur modo adorabilis est Beata Virgo ratione extrinseca id est, quatenus Christum tetigit, ita ut tota ratio hujus adorationis sit Christus. Loquitur autem de adoratione Latriae, respective saltem & secundariae, quam hujusmodi ratio, juxta ipsum, exigit. Et propterea statim subjungit, Est tamen observandum, quanquam haec ratio speculative considerata sufficiens sit ut propterea Virgo sit adorabilis: practice tamen, seu in usu non esse hoc modo adorandam praesertim communi, ac publica Ecclesiae adoratione, non quia hoc sit intrinsece malum, nam revera non est. Nam si quis idoneus sit ad discernendas rationes adorationis, & cavendum omne periculum, & ad scandalum vitandum, nulla est in hujusmodi adoratione deordinatio, aut malitia. Qui tamen communem hujus adorationis usum vitandum esse dicit tum propter periculum ne quis Virgini divinam excellentiam tribuat: tum quod major est honor personae adoratae, quod propter intrinsecam & propriam excellentiam, absolute colatur adoratione quadam inferiori, quam si adoretur, Latria respectiva propter personae divinae contactum. Proinde vult ut Virgo communiter adoretur propter alias rationes, nempe tum propter intrinsecam sanctitatem quam habet, tum propter dignitatem matris Dei, quibus Respondet cultus Latria inferior, & a Latria distinctus. In tertiam partem Thomae quaest. 37. Art. 4. disput. 22. sect. 2.
pass_a_gloss: To which doctrine are agreeable the things that are read in Francis Suárez, also a most celebrated Jesuit. For inquiring for what reason chiefly the Blessed Virgin is to be adored, he teaches that a threefold reason of adoration can be understood in the Virgin. And the first reason for which the Virgin can be adored he says is extrinsic, such as is found in the cross or nails of Christ. For just as, he says, the cross both touched Christ and was an instrument of our Redemption, so far more perfectly the most Blessed Virgin both touched Christ and cooperated toward our Redemption. In this way therefore the Blessed Virgin is adorable by an extrinsic reason, that is, insofar as she touched Christ, so that the whole reason of this adoration is Christ. But he speaks of the adoration of Latria, at least respective and secondary, which such a reason, according to him, requires. And therefore he at once subjoins that it is nevertheless to be observed that although this reason, considered speculatively, is sufficient that the Virgin be therefore adorable: yet in practice, or in use, she is not to be adored in this way, especially by the common and public adoration of the Church—not because this is intrinsically evil, for in truth it is not. For if anyone is fit to discern the reasons of adoration, and to avoid all danger, and to shun scandal, there is no disorder or malice in such adoration. Yet he says the common use of this adoration is to be avoided both because of the danger that someone attribute divine excellence to the Virgin, and because greater is the honor of the person adored when she is absolutely cultivated for her intrinsic and proper excellence with a certain inferior adoration, than if she is adored with respective Latria because of contact with the divine person. Accordingly he wills that the Virgin be commonly adored for other reasons, namely both for the intrinsic sanctity she has, and for the dignity of mother of God, to which answers a cult inferior to Latria and distinct from Latria. On the third part of Thomas, question 37, article 4, disputation 22, section 2.
pass_b_english: Suárez too allows extrinsic contact-latria—Mary touched Christ and cooperated in redemption more than cross or nails.
Speculatively fine; publicly he bars common use lest divine excellence be ascribed, and lest inferior absolute cult for her own holiness and maternity be the greater honor.

lemmas.gloss: yet in practice, or in use
